chunk_map.heading: Read the sharpen with a skeptical eye

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
Live-demo beats survive a text read.
Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 9 "Next": lines 101-103: all three bullets open with a bolded full sentence ("**Does the agent hold private data?**", "**Does untrusted content reach its context window?**", "**Is there a channel out?**") — each bold spans the whole question (6-7 words), the every-bullet-opens-bolded monoculture the rule names as the pre-2026-07-09 violation shape. chunk 10 "Bring to Module 4": line 111: "**One scoped task you'd send off rather than nudge bit by bit: a real slice with a 'done' you can name in a sentence. Bigger than a typo-fix, smaller than an epic.**" — two full sentences bolded as the entire lead, not a ≲5-word sub-span; the sibling `## Bring to Module N` sections in prework.md, run-the-first-experiment.md and learn-from-the-test.md use plain unbolded prose leads for the same section, so this reads as one-file drift rather than an established convention.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Flatten the trifecta bullets and the M4 hand-off lead to plain prose, or bold only a short handle (e.g. "private data", "untrusted content", "channel out", "one scoped task").

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
